title: Rental Period Values of Home Oxygen Therapy — Breaks in Need and Coverage Entry
content:
# Rental Period Values — Home Oxygen Therapy

Three values per system class govern how a Home Oxygen Therapy payment period reacts to a break in need and to a new primary coverage.

| System class | Break in need, beyond the days left in the month it began, after which a new payment period must start (days) | What a new payment period after a long break needs | What a patient already on oxygen needs when a new primary coverage starts paying |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stationary Concentrator Oxygen (E1390) | 60 | a new qualifying test and a new written order | a qualifying test within the lookback |
| Concentrator with Portable Cylinders (E1390 + E0431) | 60 | a new qualifying test and a new written order | a qualifying test within the lookback |
| Concentrator with Home Fill System (E1390 + K0738) | 60 | a new qualifying test and a new written order | a qualifying test within the lookback |
| Concentrator with Portable Oxygen Concentrator (E1390 + E1392) | 60 | a new qualifying test and a new written order | a qualifying test within the lookback |
| Liquid Oxygen System (E0439 + E0434) | 60 | a new qualifying test and a new written order | a qualifying test within the lookback |
| High-Flow Concentrator with Portable Cylinders (E1390 + E0431) | 60 | a new qualifying test and a new written order | a qualifying test within the lookback |

## Explanatory notes

- The break figure is counted in days of a break in need, beyond the days left in the month in which the break began; once it is exceeded, a new payment period must start.
- The requirement for a new payment period after a long break is the single value "new test and order": a new qualifying test and a new written order.
- The requirement on entry of a new primary coverage is the single value "qualifying test within lookback": a qualifying test within the lookback.

## Reading the table

**Does any class carry a different break figure?** No; every class carries 60 days, extended by the days remaining in the month in which the break began.

**Does a long break and a change of primary coverage need the same thing?** No. A new payment period after a long break needs both a new qualifying test and a new written order; a new primary coverage needs a qualifying test within the lookback.
